Class OptionsGuard

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.client.OptionsGuard
final class OptionsGuard extends Object
Puts the game options into the state the agent's vision and controls assume, and puts them back afterwards. The previous values are also written to disk, so a crash or a killed game cannot leave the player stuck with the training settings: they are restored on the next launch.

    • QUIET_DISTANCE

      private static final int QUIET_DISTANCE
      Training without the screen: how far the world is loaded and kept running around the player, in chunks. The server runs everything in that radius on every tick, and nothing in it but the arena matters, so the smaller it is the more ticks a second the fights get. Five is the least the game allows for the second of the two.

    • applyQuiet

      static void applyQuiet(net.minecraft.client.Minecraft mc)
      Training without the screen: nothing the agent sees depends on the options, so only two are touched. The game must not pause when the player looks at another window, and it need not spend the computer's strength on drawing.

    • apply

      static void apply(net.minecraft.client.Minecraft mc, int fov, boolean fast)
      Parameters:
      fov - the vertical field of view to hold the game at
      fast - the game is going to run faster than real time, so it draws as fast as it can

    • setFog

      private static void setFog(boolean on)
      The game's own switch for fog (the one its debug key flips). It is not an option and is not saved anywhere: a game that is closed while it is off starts with fog again.

    • hold

      static void hold(net.minecraft.client.Minecraft mc)
      Every tick of a session: puts the field of view back if it was changed in the options meanwhile. A network that has learned how large an opponent looks at each range is lost on any other.
